description: Centralised runtime configuration for run_full_project.ps1. RunMode selects one of the named profiles below.

phase1_v2_kg_only.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 arm C: KG prior only versus paired tabula rasa. Fixed 3000-episode horizon, strict ordered scenario IDs, paired RNG, first-goal presentations and benchmark metric schema v2.

phase1_v2_redundancy_only.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 registry-only redundancy control versus paired tabula rasa.

phase1_v2_brick_only.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 knowledge-ladder control (registered in docs/registrations/phase1_brick_only_registration_2026-11-10.md): Brick-structure-only KG prior versus paired tabula rasa. Byte-identical to phase1_v2_kg_only except stereo_knowledge_layer=brick — the ql_true arm's StereotypeReasoner reads only pre-existing vocabularies (WoT contract + brick:isLocatedIn / brick:feeds + SOSA/QUDT observation typing); no Elementary (elem:) mechanism triple is consulted, so no action is IV-gated (Rule 2 / IV-unsat prior never fire), cross-zone arcs are untyped PRIMARY, energyCost=0, no power gates. Structural claims (affectedZones, redundancy) are identical to the full arm (BrickOnlyKnowledgeLayerTest). Delta(kg_only - brick_only) isolates what the Elementary layer adds beyond Brick structure.

phase1_v2_baseline.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 arm A negative control: both arms have no KG prior, PBRS or adaptive trust.

phase1_v2_pbrs_only.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 arm B control: PBRS on, KG prior and adaptive trust off.

phase1b_v2_baseline.note: PHASE 1B arm 1 (registered 2026-07): tabula-rasa negative control, learning flags copied from phase1_v2_baseline. Protocol v2, fixed 3000-episode horizon, ordered scenario IDs, paired RNG common-seed-v1.

phase1b_v2_redundancy_only.note: PHASE 1B arm 2: ontology-free registry-only redundancy control, learning flags copied from phase1_v2_redundancy_only.

phase1b_v2_kg_frozen.note: PHASE 1B arm 3: FROZEN stereotype consumer — Q-initialisation and prior consumer byte-identical to phase1_v2_kg_only (same learning_overrides; the Phase-1b relevance/direction knobs stay at their 0.0 defaults and MUST NEVER be set here).

phase1b_v2_extended.note: PHASE 1B arm 4: EXTENDED consumer — identical to phase1b_v2_kg_frozen plus the explicitly registered relevance (stereo_irrelevant_dv_prior) and target-direction band-mirror (stereo_band_mirror_init/prior) channels. Values frozen pre-pilot; results from this arm must never be attributed to the frozen Phase-1 agent.

phase4_v2.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 Phase 4 (dependency + energy ladder). Arm-C convention (KG prior only: PBRS off, adaptive trust off — the withdrawn phase4 record stacked PBRS+trust, the same arm-D confound the Phase-1 correction eliminated) plus the non-fading lab5 energy prior. Fixed 3000-episode horizon, strict ordered scenario IDs, paired RNG, benchmark metric schema v2, and deterministic policy-energy weights for the Phase-4 actuators (ineff 4, eff 1, spotlight 2, plugs/breaker/blinds 0, lamps 1; mirrors phase4.power_formula and the KG ws:energyCost declarations).

phase4_v2_redundancy_only.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 Phase-4 knowledge-ladder control A1 (registered in docs/registrations/phase4_knowledge_ladder_registration_2026-11-13.md): registry-only redundancy prior versus paired tabula rasa on the dependency labs. Byte-identical to phase4_v2 except stereo_redundancy_only=true — the ql_true arm keeps only Rule 1 (actuator already in the commanded state) and the redundant-action soft prior; no power gate, IV gate, cross-zone, shared-actuator, or constructive-bonus rule fires. Dispatched on lab4, lab4dual, lab4chain only: on lab5 this layer would still read ws:energyCost through the full enrichment query and receive the non-fading energy prior, so lab5 is out of scope for this arm.

phase4_v2_brick_only.note: CORRECTED PROTOCOL V2 Phase-4 knowledge-ladder control A2 (registered in docs/registrations/phase4_knowledge_ladder_registration_2026-11-13.md): Brick-structure-only KG prior versus paired tabula rasa. Byte-identical to phase4_v2 except stereo_knowledge_layer=brick — the ql_true arm's StereotypeReasoner reads the WoT contract, brick:isLocatedIn / brick:feeds, and SOSA/QUDT observation typing; no ws:powerGates, ws:energyCost, or Elementary mechanism triple is consulted, so no action is power-gated or IV-gated, energyCost is 0 (the energy prior weight is inert), and cross-zone arcs are untyped. On the dependency labs the structure-only layer also claims that a plug or breaker located in a zone affects that zone's illuminance; that over-approximation is a property of the arm and is stated in the registration.

phase2.description: Phase 2 fault-detection / blacklist / re-learn (run_phase2_adapt.ps1 + .github/workflows/phase2.yml). Each adapt profile injects one or more component faults into the named parent clean lab, warm-loads that lab's clean Phase-1 Q-table (qtable_final_stereotypes_<bool><clean_source_suffix>.csv), then runs the adapt agent (taskAdapt) which detects each defect via the KG Expected-vs-Actual check, blacklists BOTH polarities of every broken component (iteratively), and re-learns over the survivors. Recovery = reconverge_episode - detect_episode (lower is better; the headline compares ql_true < ql_false). Single-fault (f1*) and multi-fault (f2*) variants span lab1/lab2/lab3 complexities and {dead, inverted} fault modes, over BOTH mechanism classes: CAUSES lamps (passive Expected-vs-Actual detection) and Mediates blinds (Phase 2.4+ — detected via the active OPEN self-test probe under sun rank >= 2; f1b* single-blind cells, and the Phase 2.7 exploratory multi-blind cell lab3_f2bdead, pre_registration.md 9.11). lab1_f1dead is degenerate (single actuator; the blacklist guard preserves the last actuator) so it is a detection-only showcase with recovery=N/A. Parent ports/flows are reused because only one faulty variant runs at a time.

adapt_settings.description: Named learning-settings profiles for the fault stage (run_phase2_adapt.ps1 -SettingsProfile, phase2.yml input settings_profile). 'properties' are passed to the adaptation JVM as -P<key>=<value> exactly as written (every key must be in the build.gradle forwarding list). 'expected' lists the effective value of every learning setting the adaptation JVM reports in its log; the runner reads them back after each cell and refuses to write the ADAPT_OK receipt on any mismatch. prior_decay 'auto' means the knowledge-preference fade length is set by the agent to a quarter of the fault-stage budget, so stereo.priorDecayEpisodes must never be passed here.

record.description: The settings every archived fault-stage run used: reward limit 50, automatic fade of the knowledge preference (a quarter of the fault-stage budget), arm-specific random stream. Reproduces the archived fault-stage results byte for byte.

paired.description: As record, but both arms use the same random stream (the arm constant is not mixed into the seed).

aligned.description: As paired, plus the reward limit of healthy training (200). The fade of the knowledge preference stays automatic (a quarter of the fault-stage budget).

phase3.description: Phase 3 process dynamics / response-delay learning (run_phase3_dynamics.ps1 + .github/workflows/phase3.yml). Each slow profile is a clean Phase-1 parent (lab2/lab3) whose simulator gives the motorized blind a temporal response delay (blind_delay_ticks env ticks). The dynamics agent (taskDynamics) runs N controlled probe trials per actuator: it pins a baseline via /setState, reads the Tick clock, toggles ONE actuator ON, then polls until the target zone illuminance rank is reached, measuring the delay in ticks. responseDelaySeconds = ticks * seconds_per_tick. Per-actuator Welford statistics are written to a separate Turtle file (learned_dynamics_<bool>_<profile>.ttl, property ws:responseDelay) that no program reads back, and to a delay table (dynamics_delays_<bool>_<profile>.csv). The agent then runs a time-bounded benchmark: for each (zone, target rank, deadline) goal it chooses actuators using the delays it has just measured, held in memory (mode ql_true), or assuming zero delay (mode ql_false); tight deadlines (< blind delay) force the fast lamp, loose deadlines admit the cheap blind. Headline metrics: delay-learning accuracy (learned vs ground-truth blind_delay_ticks) and deadline-compliance rate + energy (ql_true should meet tight deadlines and use less energy on loose ones). Dedicated ports/ontologies keep Phase 1/2 untouched.
phase3.blind_delay_tolerance_note: run_phase3_dynamics.ps1 reads the true blind delay from the started flow ('var DELAY = <ticks>;'), stops when it differs from blind_delay_ticks, and checks every learned blind delay against it: |learned - true| <= blind_delay_tolerance_ticks. One tick is the resolution of the probe (the lamp, which acts at once, is measured at about 1 tick). In the archived run of record every single blind estimate is within 0.5 ticks of 12 (mean errors 1.0-1.6 percent), and 3-probe smoke runs gave 12.0-12.33, so 1.0 tick leaves room for timing jitter while a simulator whose blinds act more than one tick earlier or later than its flow file says fails the cell.
phase3.timebounded_goals_note: Canonical time-bounded exploit goals. These are mirrored as tb_goal/4 facts in src/agt/illuminance_controller_agent_dynamics.asl (keep in sync). Each goal = a target zone illuminance rank that must be reached within a wall-clock-equivalent deadline (seconds). Sun is pinned high (900) so the motorized blind is EFFECTIVE; the only differentiator is its response delay vs the deadline. blind_delay_ticks(12) * seconds_per_tick(5) = 60 s, so deadlines < 60 s are 'tight' (only the instantaneous lamp/spotlight can meet them) and deadlines >= 60 s are 'loose' (the cheap blind also qualifies). The KG-primed arm (ql_true) uses the LEARNED per-actuator delay; the tabula-rasa arm (ql_false) assumes zero delay (no knowledge) and therefore always prefers the cheapest actuator, missing tight deadlines.

phase1b.note: PHASE 1B knowledge-necessity package (branch phase1b-labs-2026-07). Profiles: the labrel stateless relevance ladder (labrel0/4/8/16) + the fixed-K statefulness comparison (labrel8s), labband exact-band control with honest decreasing physics, and the lab4chain3 depth-3 dependency lab. Arms: the four phase1b_v2_* run modes (baseline / redundancy_only / kg_frozen / extended). Dispatch via .github/workflows/phase1.yml with explicit profiles/run_mode inputs; benchmark modes as listed.

phase4.description: Phase 4 hidden-dependency + energy labs (run via .github/workflows/phase4.yml, reusing run_full_project.ps1 with -OnlyProfiles <lab> and -RunMode phase4_v2). Four STRICTLY-CLEAN labs extend the Phase-1 clean ladder with KG-encoded knowledge a tabula-rasa learner cannot see. DEPENDENCY LADDER (cells vary how many components carry a dependency and how deep the chain is): lab4 (ONE smart-plug AND-gate: the Z1 ceiling lamp emits light only when both its switch AND SmartPlug_Z1 are ON; the KG declares ws:powerGates and the reasoner gates the lamp's ON action on the plug state by reusing the IV-gate machinery), lab4dual (TWO parallel plug dependencies: each zone's lamp behind its own plug — two ws:powerGates arcs), lab4chain (DEPTH-2 serial chain: circuit breaker gates the plug, the plug gates the Z1 lamp — two chained ws:powerGates arcs, so the lamp needs breaker AND plug AND switch all ON). ENERGY: lab5 (two directly-actionable lamps per zone with identical +400 lux output but different ws:energyCost 1 vs 4; energy is NOT in the Q-reward, so only the KG-primed agent — via the non-fading energy prior stereo_energy_prior_weight — prefers the efficient lamp / zero-energy blinds). The headline is the within-lab ql_true (KG-primed) vs ql_false (tabula-rasa) delta on first-goal episode, learning AUC, redundant-action count, goal rate, energy, and (lab5) energy-budget compliance. Statistical treatment mirrors phase1/phase3: paired across seeds, Wilcoxon signed-rank + bootstrap 95% CIs + BH-FDR + Cliff's delta. lab5 compliance is scored at benchmark time from the deterministic steady-state power of the final actuator configuration recorded in bench_step_log_<mode>.csv (power = Z1Eff*1 + Z1Ineff*4 + Z2Eff*1 + Z2Ineff*4 + Spotlight*2); compliant = GoalReached AND power <= energyBudget (per-scenario, default 2). The dependency labs carry no energyBudget, so phase4_energy.py collapses their compliance to goal_rate and the learning-speed/redundancy story comes from sweep_report.py. BenchmarkLogger CSV schema is UNCHANGED so Phases 1-3 outputs are untouched.
